Annotators (doctor and medical students) rated summaries 1‑5 on relevance, consistency, fluency, and coherence, and assessed factual recall and omission rates.

The evaluation metrics included: Clinical Evaluation Score: The doctor and the team assigned ratings ranging from 1 (poor) to 5 (good), evaluating the summaries based on overall relevance, consistency, fluency, and coherence, Medical Fact-Based Metrics: Factual Recall and Omission Recall metrics were employed to measure how well the generated summary captured medical facts compared to the gold standard annotated summary.
